edits.hypothesis: Making the user's output contract explicit in the system prompt, inlining reusable short-answer rules as a skill, and appending a one-turn reminder immediately before the first LLM call improves bare short-answer compliance on the cheapest possible attempt, before any retry or cleaning is needed.

A context-gated deterministic cleaner strips only surface wrappers (lead-ins, trailing glosses, punctuation) and extracts the requested head for recurring factual-person, role/title, and pair/list clue shapes. It fixes exact-match violations without changing the selected entity and without spending an extra LLM call.

A bounded correction loop keeps the primary model as the sole author of every rewrite (per-trigger feedback, including definition/category-vs-example guidance, plus a global final-continue cap) and uses a side model only for verdicts. It targets overexpanded short forms, non-context phrases, hyphen/space surface mismatches, single-token inflection gaps, missing monetary constraints, and wrong-entity selection without infinite re-rolls; agent.yaml wires the loop into final-answer processing.

The correction loop's automatic full-name/company shortening is the measured cause of these regressions. Restricting short-form retries to explicit short-name requests (surname/nickname/acronym/initials/known-as) and protecting full-name demo clues in the side verifier preserves the canonical surface form without changing the selected entity.

Adding reusable skill rules for quoted-fragment disambiguation, category-vs-example selection for 'these/one of these' clues, and context fallback after tool failure keeps the primary model grounded on the first attempt, without extra LLM calls or new tools.

The correction loop currently treats type-of clues as short-form requests and gives question-shape-agnostic feedback, which the traces show over-shortens specific-type answers and lets retries echo quoted phrases or repeat qualifiers. Removing the type-of over-shortening trigger and making the retry and side-verifier feedback distinguish type-of from definition/category and these/one-of-these clues keeps the primary model's bounded correction on the correct entity and surface form.

Adding a short question-shape directive to the existing turn-1 format reminder makes the already-written skill rules salient at the cheapest possible attempt. It targets definition/category, type-of, one-of-these/these, and declarative person clues before any retry or cleaning is needed, reducing wrong-entity selection and canonical-surface-form errors.

edits.hypothesis: The incumbent's rule 3 tells the model to choose the most specific attached fact, which steers bare-name/list queries toward unique single-document details and role/descriptive phrases instead of the shortest label attached in the title or lead sentence. Replacing that clause with a context-driven shared-label preference is reusable: it prefers an exact label that appears with the input in the same sentence/title/lead and is repeated across documents, while still forbidding role/title/office phrases, descriptive categories, and demographic facts. This should recover the country/state label for titled or place-name inputs without any entity-type surface mapping.

The incumbent's pronoun rule overcorrects: 'do not answer with the described object' makes the model substitute a named actor for the described character. Amending rule 4 to resolve the pronoun to the entity the predicate directly characterizes (a named person, a titled character or role, or the described thing itself) is reusable and preserves the original pronoun-resolution protection while allowing character/role answers. It keeps document titles and outside-memory names forbidden and only removes the overbroad clause that caused the regression.
